background: Intesa Sanpaolo is Italy's largest bank, funded by Italian retail deposits and lending to Italian households and companies, with large wealth management and insurance arms and a smaller international network in Central and Eastern Europe.
synthesis: Intesa Sanpaolo is rated A- on average across all three main agencies, the weakest of them at BBB+, one on a positive outlook and two on a stable outlook, after a one-notch upgrade by one of the three on 25 Nov 2025. The weak spot is CET1 of 13.0%, in the bottom quarter of EU and Nordic banks, and liquidity is thin by the same measure, with LCR of 138% in the bottom quarter and NSFR of 120% below the peer median; leverage of 5.7% is above the median. None of the ratios has moved materially over the past four periods (figures to 30 Jun 2026). The newest flagged item, on 25 Sep 2026, is a reported €95 million fraud on a bank chair in Italy using AI-faked calls, set against record quarterly earnings and a rating upgrade in the weeks before.
